note: EIGHTY-THREE SESSIONS, FIVE OF THEM TRANSCRIBED AND SEVENTY-EIGHT SYNTHESIZED, AND THE SPLIT IS STATED HERE BECAUSE NOTHING CHECKS IT. `transcribed_from` names day by day what a committed CME artifact says; `synthetic` names what this file invented around those days and on what shape. TRANSCRIBED SESSIONS: 2026-09-08, 2026-11-25, 2026-11-27, 2026-12-24, 2026-12-31. TRANSCRIBED ABSENCES, which are holidays and therefore rows that are NOT in `sessions`: 2026-09-07, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01. EVERY OTHER DAY IN THIS FILE IS SYNTHETIC: an ordinary weekday asserted by this file and by no artifact. That is 78 of the 83, so a reader who takes this calendar as a statement about the CME year is wrong about 94 percent of it. `status` stays `partial` for exactly that reason, and the seven-session note this replaced said the same thing about a smaller lie. THIS IS NOT THE PRODUCTION SEED and it is not a step toward one: `packages/db/src/seed/calendars/cme-2026-2028.source.json` still carries `holidays: null`, `generate.mjs` still refuses it on `source-not-transcribed`, and the production calendar is blocked on a retrieval this file does not perform. Two hand-maintained calendars is the drift class this corpus has found repeatedly, and this file is still the second one; what changed is that it now says which of its days a second reader could check.
what_this_format_cannot_carry: THE RECORD HAS TWO KEYS PER SESSION, `trading_day` AND `kind`, AND THE HOLIDAY SHAPES ARE MOSTLY NOT IN THEM. `golden-loader/src/calendar.ts` maps `kind` to `CalendarDay.isHalfDay` and refuses a third spelling, so an EARLY CLOSE does reach the engine: 2026-11-27 and 2026-12-24 are `half` and R-03 sees them. NOTHING ELSE HERE REACHES THE ENGINE. A HOLIDAY IS AN ABSENCE, not a row, because the record has no holiday key and a fabricated session would be worse than a missing one; what the fold sees is that 2026-11-26 is not a session and that 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-27 are adjacent in `sequence` while being two calendar days apart, which is R-02's distinction and the one a holiday gap is good for. AND ABSORPTION IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE AT ALL. ADR-055's `absorbs_into` is about the instant a session OPENS, the record states no open and no close, and `advanceDay` reads neither, so the absorbed Sunday open of 2026-09-08 and the absorbed Wednesday open of 2026-11-27 are recorded in `transcribed_from` as evidence and are invisible to every rule in the fold. A record key plus a loader mapping would be needed to change that, which is `halted`'s blocker exactly (GS-004, GS-031), and it would still not reach a rule: R-01 is the rule an open instant is for, `DailyMark` carries no timestamp, and R-01 is one of the four rules the engine does not declare because it is discharged at ingest.

labor_day.2026-09-07: HOLIDAY, so it is absent from `sessions`. No product column for 09-07 carries a trade date of 09-07 at all; every entry in that column names trade date 2026-09-08.
labor_day.2026-09-08: FULL session, closing 16:00 CT, and ITS SESSION OPENED SUNDAY 2026-09-06 AT 17:00 CT. Interest Rates, Equities and FX all read `17:00 Trade Date: 2026-09-08 (OPEN)` in the 2026-09-06 column, where an ordinary Sunday would open trade date Monday 09-07. THE MID-WEEK HOLIDAY IS ABSORBED: 09-07's session does not exist and 09-08's reaches back a day further than an ordinary Tuesday's would.
labor_day.kind_in_this_file: 2026-09-08 is `full`. The absorption changes when the session opened and not whether the day is a half day.

thanksgiving.2026-11-27: EARLY CLOSE. Per-group closes in the artifact: Interest Rates and Equities 12:15 CT, Energy, FX and Metals 13:45 CT, Grains, Livestock and Lumber 12:05 CT. THE LATEST CLOSE ACROSS F-3's SIX PRODUCTS (ES, MES, NQ, MNQ from Equities, CL from Energy, GC from Metals) IS 13:45 CT, which is the figure F-3 rules a single `session_close_at` takes. AND ITS SESSION OPENED WEDNESDAY 2026-11-25 AT 17:00 CT (16:45 preopen), where an ordinary Friday opens Thursday: the mid-week Thursday holiday is ABSORBED into 11-27.
thanksgiving.kind_in_this_file: 2026-11-27 is `half`. This is the day GS-003 names by name.

christmas.2026-12-24: EARLY CLOSE. Per-group closes: Interest Rates and Equities 12:15 CT, Energy, FX and Metals 12:45 CT, Grains, Livestock and Lumber 12:05 CT, Dairy 12:00 CT. LATEST ACROSS F-3's SIX IS 12:45 CT. NOTHING REOPENS THAT EVENING: no product carries a preopen or open for trade date 2026-12-28 in the 12-24 column, apart from Cryptocurrencies at 16:01, which is not an F-3 product.
christmas.2026-12-25: HOLIDAY, absent from `sessions`, AND IT IS A FRIDAY, SO IT ABSORBS NOTHING. The next session is Monday 2026-12-28 and it opens Sunday 2026-12-27 at 17:00 CT like any other Monday. THE EVIDENCE IS NEGATIVE: the artifact ends at 12-26 and shows no 12-28 open on the 24th, so what is transcribed is that 12-28's session did NOT reach back into Thursday, not a Sunday open time the artifact never states.

new_year.2026-12-31: FULL session, closing 16:00 CT for Interest Rates, Equities, Energy, FX and Metals, WITH NOTHING AFTER IT. An ordinary Thursday reopens at 17:00 for trade date Friday; here no product opens anything, apart from Cryptocurrencies at 16:01. THE NORMAL CLOSE IS WHY THIS DAY IS `full` AND NOT `half`: New Year's Eve is not an early close, it is an ordinary session with no session behind it.
new_year.2027-01-01: HOLIDAY, absent from `sessions`, AND IT IS A FRIDAY, SO IT ABSORBS NOTHING, on the same negative evidence as 2026-12-25.

transcribed_from.the_absorption_rule_these_four_establish: A MID-WEEK HOLIDAY IS ABSORBED AND A FRIDAY HOLIDAY IS NOT. Labor Day (Monday) and Thanksgiving (Thursday) each hand their session to the next trading day, which then opens a day earlier than an ordinary session of its weekday would. Christmas (Friday) and New Year (Friday) hand nothing to anyone, because the session that would have followed them is a Monday whose ordinary open is the Sunday evening after the holiday. That is ADR-055's `absorbs_into` observed in four artifacts, and it is recorded here as prose because the fixture record has no field for it. IT IS THE PRODUCTION SEED THAT NEEDS IT, and the production seed is where the shape and its validator already live.

synthetic: SEVENTY-EIGHT OF THE EIGHTY-THREE SESSIONS ARE SYNTHETIC: every weekday in `coverage` that is not one of the five transcribed days and is not one of the four transcribed holidays. THE RULE USED TO SYNTHESIZE THEM, stated so it can be disagreed with: a weekday that is not one of the four transcribed holidays is a `full` session, and the shape assumed for it is the ordinary weekday in `packages/db/src/seed/calendars/cme-trading-hours-2026-08-16-to-2026-08-18-all-products.retrieved-2026-08-17.xlsx`, which opens at 17:00 CT on the previous day and closes at 16:00 CT. THAT ARTIFACT IS OUTSIDE `coverage` AND NO DAY IN THIS FILE IS TRANSCRIBED FROM IT; it licenses the SHAPE the synthetic days assume and nothing more. TWO SYNTHETIC DAYS ARE THE MOST EXPOSED AND ARE NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT IN THE CROWD: 2026-10-12 (Columbus Day) and 2026-11-11 (Veterans Day) are US holidays on which CME Globex is understood to trade a full session, and NO ARTIFACT WAS RETRIEVED FOR EITHER. They are declared `full` on the synthesis rule above and on nothing else, which makes them the two days in this file most likely to be wrong. NO EARLY CLOSE AND NO HOLIDAY IS SYNTHESIZED ANYWHERE: every `half` and every absence in this file is transcribed, so a reader who finds a holiday shape here can always find its artifact.
why_this_span: IT HELD SEVEN AND SEVEN COULD NOT CARRY A HOLIDAY, AN EARLY CLOSE OR AN ABSORBED SESSION. The span runs 2026-09-04 to 2027-01-04 because the four committed artifacts sit at its two ends and in its middle: Labor Day at 2026-09-07, Thanksgiving at 2026-11-26, Christmas at 2026-12-25 and New Year at 2027-01-01. 2026-09-04 is one synthetic session BEFORE the first transcribed holiday, which is what lets a fixture open an account on a session that precedes its first mark; 2027-01-04 is one synthetic session AFTER the last transcribed holiday, which is what lets the calendar answer for the day after a fixture's last mark. THE SEVEN THIS REPLACED ARE ALL STILL HERE and their reasoning is unchanged and still load bearing, so it is kept rather than summarized. BEFORE 2026-11-02: a funded fixture is handed an explicit prior anchored at `account.opened_on` and `advanceDay` refuses a mark that is not strictly after it (INV-14, R-06). So a funded account's open day must be a session that PRECEDES its first mark, and 2026-10-30 is that day. AFTER 2026-11-06: R-31 starts the consistency period on the NEXT trading day after the eval passes, and R-32 counts by sequence subtraction; both refuse with the typed `calendar_coverage_miss` when the day they need is outside the slice (ADR-049, and the miss is UNKNOWN rather than false). So a fixture may pass its eval on the last day it trades, but the calendar must still be able to answer for the day after it, and 2026-11-09 is that day. THE EIGHTY-THREE ARE STILL CONTIGUOUS, which is what keeps the loader's synthesized `sequence` (position in this array) equal to the dense calendar index, as `golden-loader/src/calendar.ts` states and as R-02's subtraction requires. CONTIGUITY IS WHY THE SPAN IS A SPAN AND NOT FOUR ISLANDS: four holiday weeks with the months between them cut out would put a hole in the array, position and calendar index would diverge, and every gap-counting fixture graded through this file would be measuring a window offset. It would also make `coverage` claim months this file does not hold, so a day in October would come back `not_a_session` rather than `outside_coverage`, and ADR-049 makes those two different answers.
derivation: STILL NOT DERIVED, AND WIDER NOW WITHOUT BEING BETTER SOURCED THAN IT SAYS. `CI-06m` asserts what can be asserted about a hand-maintained fixture: that `session_count` and the `sessions` array are two independent statements of one number and agree (83 and 83), that every session falls inside `coverage` (2026-09-04 to 2027-01-04), that no session falls on a weekend, that the file is either `partial` or names a generator, and that a named generator resolves. THIS FILE IS `partial` AND NAMES NO GENERATOR, so it passes on the first branch and the generator citation check does not apply. WHAT `CI-06m` STILL CANNOT ASSERT IS THAT THE DAYS ARE RIGHT, and the extension makes that gap larger rather than smaller: seventy-eight synthetic days is seventy-eight assertions no gate reads. The four transcribed shapes are the part a second reader can check, which is why `transcribed_from` names the artifact and the column for each one. The day the CME publication is transcribed into `packages/db/src/seed/calendars/cme-2026-2028.source.json`, this file becomes `generated_by` output and `CI-06m`'s second check regenerates and diffs it. `status: partial` is what says that has not happened; a fixture that is not `partial` and names no generator is a finding.
